# Rebuilding Onboarding

Good morning everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Over the next few minutes, I want to walk you through how our team rebuilt the onboarding experience from the ground up. When we started this project last spring, new customers were taking almost three weeks to send their first invoice.

That number surprised us. Our product is fast once you know it, but getting to know it was slow, confusing, and frankly a little lonely. People signed up full of energy and then stalled on a settings page they did not understand.

## What we learned

We interviewed forty two customers in eleven countries. We watched them set up accounts, import contacts, and connect their bank. Almost every conversation pointed to the same three problems: too many decisions up front, jargon that only made sense to us, and no clear sense of progress.

The biggest surprise was how much people valued the small details. A friendly confirmation message, a progress bar that actually moved, and a clear next step made a remarkable difference in how confident people felt.

## What we changed

First, we moved every optional decision out of the first session. You can now send an invoice before choosing a tax region, a logo, or a payment schedule. Second, we rewrote every label in plain language and tested the new wording with people who had never seen the product. Third, we added a checklist that celebrates each step instead of hiding it.

Engineering rebuilt the import flow so that a spreadsheet with ten thousand rows now loads in under four seconds. Design created a new illustration system that makes empty screens feel inviting rather than broken. Support wrote short videos that answer the questions people ask most often.

## The results

Six months later, the median time to first invoice dropped from nineteen days to under two hours. Activation went up by thirty one percent, and support tickets about setup fell by more than half. Customers started describing the product as calm, which is the word we had hoped to hear.

## Looking ahead

Next quarter we will bring the same approach to reporting and team management. We will keep interviewing customers every week, because the best ideas in this project came directly from them. Thank you for listening, and thank you to everyone who made this work possible.
